items.sentence: FY2026 was the sharpest step, with revenue up 17.8% to $331.8 billion driven by Microsoft Cloud, Azure and Microsoft 365 Commercial cloud .

passages.filing: FY2026 10-K Item 7. Management's Discussion and Analysis
passages.text: Revenue increased $50.1 billion or 18% driven by growth in Microsoft Cloud. Intelligent Cloud revenue increased driven by Azure. Productivity and Business Processes revenue increased driven by Microsoft 365 Commercial cloud. More Personal Computing revenue decreased driven by XBOX (formerly Gaming), offset in part by growth in Search advertising.

items.label: supported
items.reason: Passage attributes revenue growth to Microsoft Cloud, Azure, and Microsoft 365 Commercial cloud.

items.sentence: FY2018 net income fell 35.0% to $16.6 billion on the TCJA charge, and FY2019 rebounded 136.8% to $39.2 billion with a $2.6 billion intangible-transfer tax benefit .

passages.filing: FY2019 10-K Item 7. Management's Discussion and Analysis
passages.text: Our effective tax rate for fiscal years 2019 and 2018 was 10% and 55%, respectively. The decrease in our effective tax rate for fiscal year 2019 compared to fiscal year 2018 was primarily due to the net charge related to the enactment of the TCJA in the second quarter of fiscal year 2018 and a $2.6 billion net income tax benefit in the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2019 related to intangible property transfers. Our effective tax rate was lower than the U.S. federal statutory rate, primarily due to the tax benefit related to intangible property transfers, and earnings taxed at lower rates in foreign jurisdictions resulting from producing and distributing our products and services through our foreign regional operations centers in Ireland, Singapore, and Puerto Rico.

items.label: supported
items.reason: Passage cites TCJA charge for FY2018 net income decline and intangible-transfer tax benefit for FY2019 rebound.

items.sentence: Server products and cloud services added 11.0pp, with Azure and other cloud services growing 41% on demand across workloads .

passages.filing: FY2026 10-K Item 7. Management's Discussion and Analysis
passages.text: •Server products and cloud services revenue increased $31.0 billion or 31% driven by Azure and other cloud services. Azure and other cloud services revenue grew 41% driven by demand for services across the platform with continued growth across all workloads. Server products revenue increased 1% primarily driven by higher purchases of licenses running in multi-cloud environments, offset in part by continued customer shift to cloud.

items.label: supported
items.reason: Passage states Azure and other cloud services grew 41% driven by demand across workloads.

items.sentence: Microsoft 365 Commercial products and cloud services added 5.1pp, with cloud revenue up 17% on Copilot and E5 revenue per user .

passages.filing: FY2026 10-K Item 7. Management's Discussion and Analysis
passages.text: •Microsoft 365 Commercial products and cloud services revenue increased $14.2 billion or 16%. Microsoft 365 Commercial cloud revenue grew 17% with growth in revenue per user driven by Microsoft 365 Copilot and Microsoft 365 E5. Microsoft 365 Commercial seats grew 6% driven by small and medium businesses and frontline worker offerings. Microsoft 365 Commercial products revenue grew 13% driven by growth in the Windows Commercial on-premises components of Microsoft 365 suite sales, as well as an increase in Office 2024 transactional purchasing.

items.label: supported
items.reason: Passage attributes Microsoft 365 Commercial cloud revenue growth to Copilot and E5 revenue per user.

items.sentence: Intelligent Cloud gross margin percentage fell on continued AI infrastructure investment and mix shift to Azure, partly offset by Azure efficiency gains .

passages.filing: FY2026 10-K Item 7. Management's Discussion and Analysis
passages.text: •Gross margin increased $13.8 billion or 21% driven by growth in Azure. Gross margin percentage decreased driven by the continued investments in AI infrastructure as well as sales mix shift to Azure, offset in part by efficiency gains in Azure.

items.label: supported
items.reason: Passage cites AI infrastructure investment and mix shift to Azure, offset by Azure efficiency gains.

items.sentence: Operating expenses rose 7.4%, driven by R&D compute capacity, AI talent, XBOX impairment and Copilot advertising .

passages.filing: FY2026 10-K Item 7. Management's Discussion and Analysis
passages.text: Operating expenses increased $4.9 billion or 7% driven by continued investments in research and development compute capacity, AI talent, and data to support product development that benefits the entire portfolio, impairment and other related expenses in our XBOX business, investments in commercial sales, and higher Copilot advertising expenses.

items.label: supported
items.reason: Passage lists R&D compute capacity, AI talent, XBOX impairment, and Copilot advertising as drivers.

items.sentence: Net margin jumped 4.2pp to 40.3% partly on $6.5 billion of OpenAI investment gains in other income .

passages.filing: FY2026 10-K Item 7. Management's Discussion and Analysis
passages.text: Other income (expense), net included $6.5 billion of net gains and $4.8 billion of net losses for fiscal years 2026 and 2025, respectively, from investments in OpenAI, primarily net recognized gains (losses) on our equity method investment reflected in Other, net. The net gains recorded for fiscal year 2026 primarily relate to the dilution gain from the OpenAI Recapitalization.

items.label: supported
items.reason: Passage notes $6.5 billion OpenAI investment gains in other income, supporting net margin increase.

items.sentence: Capex ran at 3.38x D&A and 34.9% of revenue, with investing outflow up $66.9 billion mainly on a $51.4 billion increase in property and equipment additions .

passages.filing: FY2026 10-K Item 7. Management's Discussion and Analysis
passages.text: Cash from operations increased $46.8 billion to $182.9 billion for fiscal year 2026, primarily due to an increase in cash received from customers and a decrease in cash used to pay income taxes, offset in part by an increase in cash paid to suppliers. Cash used in financing increased $847 million to $52.5 billion for fiscal year 2026, primarily due to a $6.0 billion decrease in cash used for repayments of debt, offset in part by a $3.9 billion increase in common stock repurchases and a $2.4 billion increase in dividends paid. Cash used in investing increased $66.9 billion to $139.5 billion for fiscal year 2026, primarily due to a $51.4 billion increase in additions to property and equipment and a $22.2 billion increase in cash used in other investing primarily to facilitate the purchase of components, offset in part by a $4.2 billion decrease in cash used in the acquisition of companies, net of cash acquired and divestitures, and purchases of intangible and other assets and a $2.4 billion decrease in cash used in net investment purchases, sales, and maturities.

items.label: supported
items.reason: Passage states investing outflow increased $66.9 billion mainly due to $51.4 billion property and equipment additions.
